items.stem: In the hot springs of the Puga Valley in Ladakh, temperatures remain nearly at the boiling point of water despite the cold climate. Which of the following types of organisms predominantly inhabit these extreme environmental conditions?
items.answer: Hot springs in the Puga Valley of Ladakh maintain very high temperatures even in cold climates. The organisms living in these extreme environments are mostly heat-loving bacteria called thermophiles. These unicellular organisms survive conditions similar to early Earth, helping scientists understand the origin of cellular life forms in harsh habitats.

items.stem: What is the standard limit of resolution of the human eye when viewing two tiny objects from a distance of 25 centimetres?
items.answer: The limit of resolution of the human eye is defined as the minimum distance at which two closely placed objects appear distinct. When viewed from twenty-five centimetres, two points separated by about zero point one millimetres can be seen clearly. If they are placed closer, they appear as one point. items.stem: Who was the first person to observe cell structures using a self-designed microscope while examining a thin slice of cork in the year 1665?
items.answer: In the year sixteen sixty-five, English scientist Robert Hooke used a self-designed microscope to examine a thin slice of cork. He observed small, box-like compartments that resembled tiny rooms. He coined the term cells for these structures, marking a significant milestone in biology and the beginning of widespread microscopic exploration.

items.stem: A student observes an onion peel under a light microscope. The visible circular field of view has a measured diameter of 6000 micrometres. If exactly 30 cells are aligned perfectly along this diameter, what is the estimated actual size of a single onion cell?
items.answer: To calculate the actual size of a single cell under a microscope, divide the total diameter of the visible field by the number of cells spanning that diameter. Here, the visible field diameter is six thousand micrometres. Dividing this by thirty cells gives an estimated actual cell size of two hundred micrometres.

items.stem: A cell placed in a hypertonic solution actively absorbs water and swells significantly. Which of the above statements is/are scientifically correct?
items.answer: In an isotonic solution, the concentration of the extracellular medium perfectly matches the intracellular medium, resulting in no net movement of water. items.stem: In biological systems, the net movement of molecular particles from a region of higher concentration to a region of lower concentration occurs spontaneously. What is the specific term used when this exact process involves the critical diffusion of water molecules strictly across a selectively permeable membrane?
items.answer: Diffusion is the net movement of particles from a region of higher concentration to a lower concentration until equilibrium is reached. It can occur in any medium and does not require a membrane. Osmosis is specifically the targeted diffusion of water molecules across a selectively permeable membrane along a concentration gradient. items.stem: Unlike complex eukaryotic cells, primitive bacterial cells completely lack a true membrane- bound nucleus. Instead, their genetic material typically exists as a single continuous circular DNA molecule. items.answer: Prokaryotic cells, such as basic bacteria, fundamentally lack a well-defined, membrane- bound nucleus to house their genetic material. Instead, their DNA exists as a single circular molecule freely suspended within the cytoplasm. This specific, undefined central region containing the vital genetic material is scientifically referred to as the nucleoid in prokaryotic organisms.

items.stem: The nucleus centrally contains genetic material crucial for the ongoing inheritance of traits. items.answer: Inside a non-dividing eukaryotic cell, essential DNA is loosely present as an entangled mass of thread-like structures known as chromatin. However, whenever the cell prepares to undergo division, this loose chromatin material tightly condenses and neatly organizes itself into distinct rod-shaped structures universally recognized by scientists as discrete cellular chromosomes.

items.answer: The plant cell wall is a rigid outer covering composed primarily of cellulose, providing essential structural support. While rigid, it remains highly permeable to water and dissolved minerals. Animal cells completely lack this structure, which is why they easily change shape and can burst when placed in highly hypotonic environments.

items.stem: Inside complex eukaryotic cells, the clear cytoplasm serves as a dynamic medium containing numerous membrane-bound organelles. items.answer: The cytoplasm is a semi-fluid substance filling the cell interior, housing all specialized organelles. In many eukaryotic cells, it also serves as a critical storage site for essential materials. These non- living stored substances, clearly known as cell inclusions, include excess starch in plant cells and specific calcium oxalate or silica crystals.

items.stem: Definitive proposal that all new biological cells continuously arise from pre-existing ones.

Later, in eighteen fifty-five, Rudolf Virchow expanded the theory by observing that new cells originate from pre-existing cells. Finally, Camillo Golgi discovered the Golgi apparatus in eighteen ninety-eight.
